messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT alert INC-2026-1887 — high 429 spike detected on dedicated pools (eu-west-1). Service: valve-proxy. Concurrency saturating pool org-12. autoscaler attempted +2 nodes but hit pool quota=4. Paging @lee_oncall and infra. Link: https://ops.redwood/incident/INC-2026-1887 :rotating_light:
lee_oncall: I'm on it, digging into autoscaler logs now. any recent deploys?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: No deploys to valve-proxy in the last 30m. Recent config change: none.
morgan_sre: looking at metrics — tenant=shopify-proxy shows 5x spike in r/s and extremely bursty short-lived requests. KV cache miss rate up ~40%. This is filling concurrency slots and preventing smooth scaling.
lee_oncall: grabbing autoscaler logs: ```2026-03-17T09:12:04Z autoscaler: scale_attempt org-12 -> +2 GPUs, reason=cpu/queue, result=quota_exceeded (4/4)
2026-03-17T09:12:12Z autoscaler: backoff 30s```
lee_oncall: confirmed: control-plane refused capacity due to hard quota at org level.
devon_infra: I can toggle burst capacity for the dedicated pool as a short-term mitigation (allows ephemeral extra slots). Proposal: enable burst for pool org-12, apply tenant-level shaping for heavy tenants, and apply soft rate-limit fallback (429s) to non-critical routes.
lee_oncall: go ahead and enable burst, devon. Post the control-plane command when you run it.
devon_infra: running: ```curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/pools/org-12/burst/enable" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"duration_s":600, "max_extra_gpus":2}'```
devon_infra: response: 200 OK — burst enabled (extra_gpus_allocated=2). Pool effective capacity now 6. :white_check_mark:
morgan_sre: nice. Also applying tenant traffic shaping — temporary limit shopify-proxy -> 120 rps and reduce concurrency slice to 0.2 of a worker for that tenant. Command: ```rbctl tenants update --id shopify-proxy --rate-limit 120 --concurrency-slice 0.2```
morgan_sre: applied.
sarah_cs: heads-up from support: multiple customers reported 429s and slower responses starting ~09:09Z. Notifying affected customers with ETA 15m for mitigation.
lee_oncall: metrics now: 429 rate from 18% -> 4% in last 120s, p95 latency down 40%. Autoscaler also now allowed to add nodes if needed.
infra-bot: autoscaler event: ```2026-03-17T09:16:28Z autoscaler: scale_success org-12 -> +1 GPU allocated (total=5)```
lee_oncall: good — keeps stabilizing. Keeping burst enabled for the next 10m while we monitor.
carla_eng: can we capture a quick snapshot of routes that triggered the most tokens/requests? I want to identify whether this is a legitimate traffic surge or a misbehaving client.
morgan_sre: snapshot (top routes by rps): ["/generate/chat", "/embed/batch", "/internal/prefetch"]. Most of the spike is on /internal/prefetch — looks like a retry storm from a worker fleet.
carla_eng: if it's a retry storm, we'll push a remediation to de-dupe and use backoff in the client. I'll open a PR for a client-side fix and coordinate rollout.
lee_oncall: action items: 1) devon - leave burst enabled for 10 more minutes and then disable if stable. 2) morgan - follow up with permanent rate policy for background/internal routes. 3) carla - investigate retry root cause and PR. 4) sarah - customer comms updated with note about burst toggle & traffic shaping.
morgan_sre: suggested permanent change: hard-rate-limit for /internal/* to 200 rps per tenant and a dedicated concurrency slice setting for background jobs. Also request quota bump for org-12 to 8 GPUs (support ticket created: #TICK-4983).
sarah_cs: I've acknowledged to affected customers and escalated OEM account. No regulatory/customer data exposure reported.
devon_infra: disabling burst in 12m unless we see renewed pressure. Command to disable: ```curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/pools/org-12/burst/disable" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"```
lee_oncall: handing off to carla_eng for postmortem + followups. I'll remain reachable for 30m, then hand to next oncall. :handshake:
carla_eng: taking postmortem ownership. I'll compile timeline, root cause (retry storm + quota), mitigations (burst enable, tenant shaping, rate-policy), and follow-ups (quota request, client fix, permanent policy).
lee_oncall: final check — error rate holding ~3% and latency stable. Closing incident channel in 20m if no regression. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-1887 status update: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident channel will archive in 24h unless reopened.
carla_eng: noted. Will post postmortem draft in #postmortems tomorrow.
